name: Learn: Gateway API (hardened)
objective: CKA › Services & Networking. Drill EVERY corner of the Gateway API harder than the exam: install the CRDs, define a GatewayClass, stand up a Gateway with a named HTTP listener scoped by allowedRoutes, attach an HTTPRoute (path match + backend), add header-based matching, rewrite request headers with a filter, split traffic by weight across two backends, contrast with Ingress, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Nine strict practicals over the whole Gateway API surface. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Install the Gateway API CRDs
questions.teach:
The Gateway API isn't built into Kubernetes — it ships as **CRDs you install** from a release manifest. Until you `kubectl apply` them, the API server rejects `Gateway`/`HTTPRoute` objects.

**Gotcha:** wait for the CRD to reach the **Established** condition before creating CRs — applying a CRD and its CR together can race.
questions.prompt:
Install the Gateway API CRDs. The standard-channel manifest is staged at `/tmp/gateway-api-crds.yaml`. Apply it so the `GatewayClass`/`Gateway`/`HTTPRoute` types exist.

Target: the `gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io` CRD is installed and reports the `Established` condition True.
questions.hint: `kubectl apply -f /tmp/gateway-api-crds.yaml`, then `kubectl get crd | grep gateway.networking.k8s.io`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -f /tmp/gateway-api-crds.yaml
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io

questions.title: GatewayClass — the infrastructure template
questions.teach:
A **GatewayClass** is cluster-scoped and names the **controller** that implements any `Gateway` referencing it, via `spec.controllerName` (a domain-prefixed path). It's the Gateway API's analogue to `IngressClass`.

**Gotcha:** `kubectl create` has **no generator** for Gateway API objects — write the YAML and `apply -f` it.
questions.prompt:
Create a cluster-scoped `GatewayClass` named `kindlab-gc` with `spec.controllerName` exactly `kindlab.io/gateway-controller`.

Target: GatewayClass `kindlab-gc` exists with controllerName `kindlab.io/gateway-controller`.
questions.hint: Apply a manifest: `apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`, `kind: GatewayClass`, `metadata.name: kindlab-gc`, `spec.controllerName: kindlab.io/gateway-controller`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata:
  name: kindlab-gc
spec:
  controllerName: kindlab.io/gateway-controller
EOF

verification.description: GatewayClass kindlab-gc exists with controllerName kindlab.io/gateway-controller

questions.title: Gateway with a named listener + allowedRoutes
questions.teach:
A **Gateway** is namespaced. It references a class via `spec.gatewayClassName` and declares **listeners** — each with a unique `name`, a `protocol`, and a `port`. A listener's `allowedRoutes.namespaces.from: Same` restricts which namespaces may attach routes.

**Gotcha:** listener `name`s must be unique within a Gateway, and the `name` is what an HTTPRoute targets via `parentRefs[].sectionName`.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `gw-learn`, create a `Gateway` named `web-gw` referencing class `kindlab-gc` with ONE listener: `name: http`, `protocol: HTTP`, `port: 80`, and `allowedRoutes.namespaces.from: Same`.

Target: Gateway `web-gw` in `gw-learn`, gatewayClassName `kindlab-gc`, listener named `http` protocol HTTP port 80 with allowedRoutes.namespaces.from=Same.
questions.hint: `spec.gatewayClassName: kindlab-gc`; `spec.listeners: [{name: http, protocol: HTTP, port: 80, allowedRoutes: {namespaces: {from: Same}}}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: web-gw
  namespace: gw-learn
spec:
  gatewayClassName: kindlab-gc
  listeners:
  - name: http
    protocol: HTTP
    port: 80
    allowedRoutes:
      namespaces:
        from: Same
EOF

verification.description: Gateway web-gw: class kindlab-gc + listener http HTTP:80 allowedRoutes from=Same

questions.title: HTTPRoute — path match + backend
questions.teach:
An **HTTPRoute** binds to a Gateway through `spec.parentRefs` and describes routing via `spec.rules` — each rule has `matches` (e.g. `path.type: PathPrefix`, `value: /`) and `backendRefs` (target Service + port). `spec.hostnames` scopes it to a host.

**Gotcha:** a typo'd backend doesn't error on apply — it surfaces as `ResolvedRefs: False` in the route's status.
questions.prompt:
In `gw-learn`, create an `HTTPRoute` named `web-route` that: attaches to Gateway `web-gw` via `parentRefs` (sectionName `http`), scopes hostname `hello.example.com`, matches path prefix `/`, and forwards to Service `hello` on port `80`. The `hello` Service (port 80) is seeded for you.

Target: web-route parentRef web-gw sectionName http, hostname hello.example.com, rule PathPrefix / → backend hello:80.
questions.hint: `spec.parentRefs: [{name: web-gw, sectionName: http}]`, `spec.hostnames: [hello.example.com]`, rule `matches[0].path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}` and `backendRefs: [{name: hello, port: 80}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: web-route
  namespace: gw-learn
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: web-gw
    sectionName: http
  hostnames:
  - hello.example.com
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path:
        type: PathPrefix
        value: /
    backendRefs:
    - name: hello
      port: 80
EOF

verification.description: web-route: parentRef web-gw/http + hostname + PathPrefix / → hello:80

questions.title: Header-based matching
questions.teach:
A match combines `path`, `method`, `headers`, and `queryParams` — ALL conditions in one `matches` entry must hold (AND). A header match is `headers: [{type: Exact, name: X, value: Y}]`.

**Gotcha:** list header matches **inside the same `matches` entry** to AND them with the path; separate `matches` entries are ORed instead.
questions.prompt:
In `gw-learn`, create an `HTTPRoute` named `canary-route` attached to `web-gw` (sectionName `http`), hostname `hello.example.com`, with ONE rule whose single match requires BOTH path prefix `/` AND header `x-env: canary` (Exact), forwarding to Service `hello-canary` on port `80`. Both `hello` and `hello-canary` Services are seeded.

Target: canary-route one match with PathPrefix / AND Exact header x-env=canary → backend hello-canary:80.
questions.hint: In the single `matches` entry put both `path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}` and `headers: [{type: Exact, name: x-env, value: canary}]`, then `backendRefs: [{name: hello-canary, port: 80}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: canary-route
  namespace: gw-learn
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: web-gw
    sectionName: http
  hostnames:
  - hello.example.com
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path:
        type: PathPrefix
        value: /
      headers:
      - type: Exact
        name: x-env
        value: canary
    backendRefs:
    - name: hello-canary
      port: 80
EOF

verification.description: canary-route: one match ANDs PathPrefix / with header x-env=canary → hello-canary:80

questions.title: Request-header filter (RequestHeaderModifier)
questions.teach:
A rule's `filters` transform traffic before it reaches the backend. `type: RequestHeaderModifier` can `set`, `add`, or `remove` request headers — `set` entries are `{name, value}` pairs.

**Gotcha:** the filter goes under `rules[].filters` (the whole rule) or `backendRefs[].filters` (that backend only) — these are different scopes; use the rule level here.
questions.prompt:
In `gw-learn`, create an `HTTPRoute` named `hdr-route` attached to `web-gw` (sectionName `http`), hostname `hello.example.com`, path prefix `/`, forwarding to `hello:80`, with a rule-level filter of type `RequestHeaderModifier` that **sets** header `x-gateway: kindlab`.

Target: hdr-route rule has filter RequestHeaderModifier set x-gateway=kindlab, backend hello:80.
questions.hint: Under the rule: `filters: [{type: RequestHeaderModifier, requestHeaderModifier: {set: [{name: x-gateway, value: kindlab}]}}]` alongside `backendRefs: [{name: hello, port: 80}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: hdr-route
  namespace: gw-learn
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: web-gw
    sectionName: http
  hostnames:
  - hello.example.com
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path:
        type: PathPrefix
        value: /
    filters:
    - type: RequestHeaderModifier
      requestHeaderModifier:
        set:
        - name: x-gateway
          value: kindlab
    backendRefs:
    - name: hello
      port: 80
EOF

verification.description: hdr-route: RequestHeaderModifier set x-gateway=kindlab + backend hello:80

questions.title: Traffic splitting by weight
questions.teach:
Put **multiple `backendRefs` in one rule** and give each a `weight` to split traffic — the controller distributes requests proportionally to the weights (they need not sum to 100).

**Gotcha:** weighting is per-rule across its `backendRefs`; a `weight: 0` backend receives no traffic but still resolves.
questions.prompt:
In `gw-learn`, create an `HTTPRoute` named `split-route` attached to `web-gw` (sectionName `http`), hostname `hello.example.com`, path prefix `/`, with ONE rule that splits across two backends: `hello:80` weight `90` and `hello-canary:80` weight `10`.

Target: split-route one rule, two backendRefs — hello:80 weight 90 and hello-canary:80 weight 10.
questions.hint: One rule with `backendRefs: [{name: hello, port: 80, weight: 90}, {name: hello-canary, port: 80, weight: 10}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: split-route
  namespace: gw-learn
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: web-gw
    sectionName: http
  hostnames:
  - hello.example.com
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path:
        type: PathPrefix
        value: /
    backendRefs:
    - name: hello
      port: 80
      weight: 90
    - name: hello-canary
      port: 80
      weight: 10
EOF

verification.description: split-route: hello:80 weight 90 + hello-canary:80 weight 10 in one rule

questions.title: Contrast with Ingress
questions.teach:
The Gateway API replaces **Ingress**, so express the same routing the old way. An Ingress is one resource whose `spec.rules[].http.paths[]` map a path to a `backend.service`. The fast generator is `kubectl create ingress NAME --rule="host/path*=svc:port"`.

**Gotcha:** a trailing `*` on the path in `--rule` → `pathType: Prefix`; without it → `Exact`.
questions.prompt:
In `gw-learn`, create an `Ingress` named `web-ing` routing host `hello.example.com` path `/` (Prefix) to Service `hello` port `80`.

Target: Ingress web-ing in gw-learn routes host hello.example.com, path / pathType Prefix, to backend Service hello port 80.

verification.description: Ingress web-ing: host hello.example.com, path / Prefix → hello:80

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a route that won't attach
questions.teach:
An HTTPRoute that applies cleanly but routes nothing usually has a **bad parentRef or backend**. Check the route's `status.parents[].conditions`: `Accepted: False` (reason `NoMatchingParent`) means the `parentRefs` name/sectionName is wrong; `ResolvedRefs: False` means a backend is missing.

**Gotcha:** fix the HTTPRoute's refs to match the real Gateway/Service — don't recreate the Gateway.
questions.prompt:
HTTPRoute `broken-route` in `gw-learn` was applied but doesn't attach — its `parentRefs` names a Gateway that doesn't exist, and its `backendRefs` names a Service that doesn't exist. Diagnose and fix it IN PLACE so it attaches to Gateway `web-gw` (sectionName `http`) and forwards to the real Service `hello` on port `80`. Do not delete and recreate from scratch.

Target: broken-route parentRef web-gw/http + backendRef hello:80.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n gw-learn get httproute broken-route -o yaml` and read `status`. Then `kubectl -n gw-learn edit httproute broken-route`: set `parentRefs[0].name: web-gw`, `sectionName: http`, and `backendRefs[0].name: hello, port: 80`.

verification.description: broken-route fixed: parentRef web-gw/http + backend hello:80
